questions.question: In a corporation election, two candidates fought for the post of Mayor. One candidate got 40% of the valid votes. 23% of the votes were invalid. If the total votes were 21000, what is the number of valid votes that the other candidate got?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total votes were 21000

One candidate got 40% of the valid votes.

23% of the votes were invalid.

**Calculation:**

Total valid votes = 21000 × (100 - 23)%

⇒ 16170

Number of valid votes got by the one candidate = 16170 × 40%

⇒ 6468

So, the number of valid votes got by the other candidate = 16170 - 6468

⇒ 9702

**∴ The number of valid votes that the other candidate got was 9702.**

questions.question: A person travels equal distances at speeds of 3 km/h, 4 km/h, 7 km/h and 12km/h, and takes a total of 680 minutes. What is the total distance (in km) travelled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let each equal distance segment be the LCM of speeds (3, 4, 7, 12) = 84 km.

Assumed total time for 4 × 84 km = (84/3) + (84/4) + (84/7) + (84/12) = 28 + 21 + 12 + 7 = 68 hours.

Actual total time given = 680 minutes = 680 ÷ 60 = 68/6 hours.

Distance multiplier = Actual Time ÷ Assumed Time = (68/6) ÷ 68 = 1/6.

Total distance = Assumed Total Distance × Multiplier = (4 × 84) × (1/6) = 336 ÷ 6 = 56 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 56 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d4fff1348c437aaf1353ab798416c0816fc3ef933ed65b7e9934221c31c7ee0c.png] 

**Given:**

Speeds of the four equal segments = 3 km/h, 4 km/h, 7 km/h, and 12 km/h.

Total time taken = 680 minutes = 680/60 hours = 34/3 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Total Distance = 4 × Distance of one segment

**Calculation:**

Let the equal distance traveled at each speed be d km.

⇒ Total distance = 4d km.

⇒ Total time = (d/3) + (d/4) + (d/7) + (d/12)

⇒ LCM of 3, 4, 7, and 12 is 84.

⇒ Total time = (28d + 21d + 12d + 7d) ÷ 84

⇒ Total time = 68d / 84 = 17d / 21 hours

According to the problem, the total time is 34/3 hours.

⇒ 17d / 21 = 34 / 3

⇒ d = (34 × 21) ÷ (17 × 3)

⇒ d = 2 × 7 = 14 km.

⇒ Total distance = 4d = 4 × 14 = 56 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 56 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for n Equal Distances

If an object covers n equal distances at speeds S₁, S₂, ... Sₙ, the average speed is given by the harmonic mean: Average Speed = n ÷ (1/S₁ + 1/S₂ + ... + 1/Sₙ).

General Average Speed Formula

For unequal distances or times, the average speed is strictly the ratio of total distance covered to the total time taken: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). If moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).

questions.question: How many numbers are there from 500 to 550 (including both) which are neither divisible by 3 nor by 11?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total numbers from 500 to 550 = 550 − 500 + 1 = 51.

Numbers divisible by 3 (501 to 549) = 17.

Numbers divisible by 11 (506 to 550) = 5.

Numbers divisible by both (33) = 1 (only 528).

Numbers divisible by 3 or 11 = 17 + 5 − 1 = 21.

Neither divisible by 3 nor 11 = 51 − 21 = 30.

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Range [500, 550], Divisors 3 and 11.

Formula Used: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B)

 
 Total (N) = 51

⇒ Total numbers (N) = 550 − 500 + 1 = 51

⇒ Divisible by 3 in [1, 550] = floor(550/3) = 183

⇒ Divisible by 3 in [1, 499] = floor(499/3) = 166

⇒ n(3) in range = 183 − 166 = 17

⇒ Divisible by 11 in [1, 550] = floor(550/11) = 50

⇒ Divisible by 11 in [1, 499] = floor(499/11) = 45

⇒ n(11) in range = 50 − 45 = 5

⇒ Divisible by both (3 × 11 = 33) = floor(550/33) − floor(499/33) = 16 − 15 = 1

⇒ Total numbers divisible by 3 or 11 = 17 + 5 − 1 = 21

⇒ Numbers neither divisible by 3 nor 11 = 51 − 21 = 30

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inclusion-Exclusion Principle

For any two sets A and B, the number of elements in their union is given by n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B).

Count of Multiples in a Range

To find multiples of k in [a, b], use: floor(b/k) − floor((a−1)/k).

Divisibility by 3 and 11

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3. It is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd and even positions is 0 or a multiple of 11.</p

Divisibility Rule of 9 = If the sum of digits of the number is divisible by 9, then the number itself is divisible by 9.

**Calculation:**

72 = 9 × 8

So, the number should be divisible by both 8 and 9

87y is divisible by 8

Only possible value of y is 2

Now,

8 + 9 + x + 6 + 4 + 0 + 2 + 0 + 8 + 7 + 2 = 46 + x is divisble by 9

In x = 8 the number = 54 which is completely diviaible by 9

Now,

⇒ 16 - 2

questions.question: A and B can finish a job in 10 days and 5 days, respectively. They worked together for 2 days, after which B was replaced by C and the job was finished in the next 3 days. In how many days will C alone finish 50% of the job?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do a job in 10 days

B can do a job in 5 days

**Concept used:**

Efficiency = Total work/Time taken

**Calculation:**

LCM of 10 and 5 = 10 i.e total work

Efficiency of A = 10/10 = 1 unit/day

Efficiency of B = 10/5 = 2 units/day

Effective efficiency of A and B = 1 + 2 = 3 units/day

A and B work for 2 days

So, work completed = 3 × 2 units

⇒ 6 units

Remaining work = (10 – 6) units

⇒ 4 units

A and C can complete the remaining work in 3 days

So, A and C's one day work = 4/3 units

C's one-day work = (4/3) – 1

⇒ 1/3 unit/day

C can complete 50% of work in (10 × 50\%)/(frac{1){3}} days

⇒ 5 × 3 = 15 days

**∴ C can complete 50% of work in 15 days.**

questions.question: On a marked price, the difference between the selling prices with a discount of 35% and two successive discounts of 20% and 15% is ₹990. The marked price of the article (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Normal Discount on selling price = 35%

Successive discount on selling price = 20% & 15%

Difference in amount of normal and successive discount = Rs. 990 

**Concept Used:**

Successive Discount formula = D1 + D2 - (D1 × D2)/100

Selling price = Marked price - Marked price × discount%

**Calculation:**

 Successive discount = 20 + 15 - (20 × 15)/100

⇒ 32%

Normal discount = 35%

Let the the marked price of the article be Rs. 100a

According to the question,

100a × 35% - 100a × 32% = Rs.990 

⇒ 100a(35% - 32%) = 990

⇒ 100a × 3% = 990

⇒ 3a = 990

⇒ a = 330

⇒ 100a = 330 × 100 = 33000

So, marked price of the article is Rs. 33000

** ∴ The marked price of the article (in ₹) is 33000.**

questions.question: When the speed of a truck is increased by 20%, it takes 25 minutes less to cover the same distance. What is the time (in hours) taken to cover twice the distance at its actual speed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

When the speed of a truck is increased by 20%, it takes 25 minutes less to cover the same distance.

**Concept used:**

Time = Distance/Speed

**Calculation:**

Let the distance be ‘x’ km and speed be ‘n’ km/minutes

So, increased speed = n × 120%

⇒ 1.2n

According to the question,

(x/n) – (x/1.2n) = 25 

⇒ [(1.2x - x)/1.2n] = 25

⇒ 0.2x/1.2n = 25

⇒ x/n = (25 × 1.2)/0.2

⇒ x/n = 30/0.2

⇒ x/n = 150

Here, ‘x/n’ is the time taken to cover the distance with the original speed.

So, to cover twice its actual distance with its actual speed will take = 150 × 2

⇒ 300 minutes

300 minutes = 5 hours [∵ 1 hour = 60 minutes]

**∴ The time (in hours) taken to cover twice the distance at its actual speed is 5.**

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum of money at the rate of 8% p.a. for 9 years is ₹2,880. At what rate of interest can the same amount of interest can be received on the same sum for 12 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Simple Interest = Rs. 2880

Rate % = 8% p.a

Time = 9 years

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest = PTR/100 

Where,

P = principal

R = rate %

T = time

**Calculation:**

Let the principal be P

According to the concept,

2880 = (P × 8 × 9)/100

⇒ 2880 = (72P)/100

⇒ P = 2880 × 100/72

⇒ P = Rs. 4000

Let rate for 12 years for same interest to be found be R 

2880 = (4000 × 12 × R)/100

⇒ 2880 = 48000R/100 

⇒ R = 2880 × 100/48000

⇒ R = 6%

**∴ The required rate percent is 6%**

questions.question: The average weight of 44 members of a club is 68.5 kg. If 6 members of average weight 72.8 kg leave and 2 new members of average weight 56.1 kg join the club, then the average weight (in kg) of the present members of the club is (correct to nearest integer):
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average weight of 44 members of a club is 68.5 kg

The average weight of 6 members who left is 72.8 kg

The average weight of 2 members who joined is 56.1kg

**Concept used:**

Average = Sum of elements/Number of elements

**Calculation:**

Total weight of 44 members = 68.5 × 44

⇒ 3014

Total weight of 6 members who left = 72.8 × 6

⇒ 436.8

Total weight of 2 members who joined = 56.1 × 2

⇒ 112.2

Total weight after 6 members left and 2 members joined = 3014 - 436.8 + 112.2

⇒ 2689.4

Number of members now = 44 - 6 + 2

⇒ 40

Average of the new group = 2689.4/40

⇒ 67.235 ≈ 67 kg

**∴ The average weight (in kg) of the present members of the club is (correct to nearest integer) is 67.**
